While Report Noisy Max typically uses Gumbel or Laplace noise to satisfy $\varepsilon$-differential privacy, it is a known result that using Exponential noise with rate $\varepsilon/\Delta$ (or scale $\Delta/\varepsilon$) also satisfies $\varepsilon$-differential privacy.

The probability of choosing item 1 is $P(Z_1 + q_1 > Z_2 + q_2) = P(Z_2 - Z_1 < \Delta q)$. Since $Z_i$ are exponential, the difference $Z_2 - Z_1$ follows a Laplace distribution with scale $\Delta/\varepsilon$.
If a neighboring dataset $D'$ shifts a score by at most $\Delta$, the argument $\Delta q$ shifts by at most $\Delta$. With $b = \Delta/\varepsilon$ and shift $\le \Delta$, the probability ratio is bounded by $e^{\Delta / (\Delta/\varepsilon)} = e^\varepsilon$.

This property holds for general $d$ as well. The Report Noisy Max mechanism with independent noise $Z_j$ drawn from $\text{Exponential}(\varepsilon/\Delta)$ satisfies $\varepsilon$-differential privacy.

Since the entries are in $[0, 1]$, $|x_k - x'_k| \le 1$.
